tei:respStmt.tei:name: Efraim Feinstein

tei:editionStmt.tei:edition: Read directly from the scanned 1949 printing, page by page

tei:div.tei:p: Master of all worlds! It is not on account of our own righteousness that we offer our supplications before thee, but on account of thy great compassion. What are we? What is our life? What is our goodness? What our righteousness? What our helpfulness? What our strength? What our might? What can we say in thy presence, Lord our God and God of our fathers? Indeed, all the heroes are as nothing before thee, the men of renown as though they never existed, the wise as if they were without knowledge, the intelligent as though they lacked understanding; for most of their doings are worthless, and the days of their life are vain in thy sight; man is not far above beast, for all is vanity.
